messages:
srinivas: Heads-up — I'm bringing juno-6b (int8) into preprod for a quick sanity + quant smoke. Want to run the usual checks: tokenization edgecases, instruction-following, stop-sequence behavior, and a tiny perf sweep. Will post prompts and short curl tests in a bit.

maya: thanks. can you drop the prompt set here? also which quant backend/config did you use?

srinivas: using our int8-runner with per-channel symmetric q, opt-level=2 (fast path). prompt set is tiny, saved to GDrive: https://gdrive.internal/redwood/juno6b/preprod-smoke.txt — main checks below.

oliver: quick note — for int8 we should watch for tokenization mismatches (esp emojis and multi-byte chars) and kv-cache regressions.

srinivas: agreed. checklist I'm running now:
- basic instruction following (3 examples)
- stop-seq enforcement (newline and custom token)
- numeric reasoning sanity (small math)
- multi-lingual sanity (en/es/zh short)
- streaming + fallback behavior
- perf: p50/p95 token lat and tps

jen: if you can, attach the curl test you run so I can replicate. and please capture raw tokens (ids) for one failing case if it looks off.

srinivas: curl test below:

```
curl -s -X POST https://preprod.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"juno-6b-int8","input":"Translate to French: Hello, how are you?","max_tokens":40,"stop":["\n"],"stream":false}'
```

srinivas: sample output (trimmed):
```
Output: "Bonjour, comment ça va ?"
Tokens: [154, 23, 891, ...]
```

maya: good. any failures so far?

srinivas: one small regression on stop-seq where a custom token stop didn't cut off reliably in the first run. Example: prompt with stop token `<END>` occasionally returned ` <END>more` (extra space + suffix).

oliver: that's likely token-alignment after quantization; might need to pin tokenizer vocab or check post-token merge logic. can you dump the token ids around the stop token?

srinivas: pinned dump for that case: tokens around stop — [2101("<"), 109("END"), 2102(">"), 45("more")]. Looks like tokenizer split `<END>` into three tokens, so our stop matching (which assumed a single token) fails.

ashley: ok actionable: update the stop matcher to handle multi-token stops (or use string-level match on detokenized output as a fallback). Also add a unit test for this exact split.

jen: perf numbers from a small throughput run (single preprod GPU, batch size=4, seq=512): p50 per-token latency ~42ms, p95 ~180ms, throughput ~220 tokens/s. memory stable at ~8.1GB (int8). fp16 baseline was p50 38ms p95 160ms.

maya: those perf diffs look acceptable but need to confirm latency SLO for streaming fallback. if p95 > 200ms we should consider fallback to fp16 for low-latency routes.

srinivas: agreed. I ran a quick correctness eval against our 30-example smoke set — accuracy on instruction-following 28/30, numeric reasoning 9/10, translation exact-match 19/20. one hallucination on a date question.

ci-bot: [automated-check] lint: ok, unit-tests: 124 passed, 2 skipped, smoke-eval: 1 failed (stop-seq multi-token). See /ci/artifacts/1713004321/smoke-report.html

oliver: since we have a deterministic token-split cause, plan: (1) implement multi-token stop matching fallback, (2) add detokenized-string fallback, (3) re-run smoke.

ashley: add eval ticket to backlog and tag qa for forced regression run. also include quant-config (opt-level, symmetric/per-channel) in the ticket.

jen: I'll re-run perf with streaming enabled and batch=1 to get tail latencies. putting a small script in the same GDrive folder.

maya: who owns the follow-ups? srinivas?

srinivas: i'll take the stop-match fix + re-run. jen will do perf streaming tails. ashley will file the ticket and tag qa. oliver will review tokenizer implications.

maya: lovely. mark as in-progress. ping if you need capacity. :thumbsup:

srinivas: thanks — starting the fix now, will post a short PR and the retest results here when done.
